solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swindle Greek character for seafood

blocks.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A menu warning: the Greek taverna is fleecing you over the seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person from Greece; in crosswords it is almost always a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustines, a staple seafood dish.

clue.text: Ridicule South African flag

blocks.note: to flag is to tire, to lose energy

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the South African national flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' reads as a banner beside 'South African', but here it is the verb: to flag is to grow tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is ridicule used to expose folly.

clue.text: On camera, I stirred coffee

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A vlogger stirs a coffee while filming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirred' is at home beside 'coffee', which hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An americano is espresso topped up with hot water.

clue.text: Model entertains small gang

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so POSE holds S

blocks.note: to model is to pose; the outer part
S = small, as on clothing labels; goes inside

explanation.surface: A fashion model hosts a little group of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun for a person, but the wordplay wants the verb: to model is to pose.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a group of people, a gang or crew.

clue.text: Prepares orthodontic device

definitions.note: 'Braces' as a verb matches 'Prepares'; as a noun it is plural, naming one device

blocks.note: to steel yourself for a shock
the wires worn on teeth to straighten them; the noun is plural

explanation.surface: Someone gets a dental brace fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings sit side by side with no link, so 'Prepares' can be mistaken for part of a sentence about fitting the device.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: you brace yourself for bad news, and the wire fitted to crooked teeth goes by the same plural word.

clue.text: Italian cheese — cook it with actor

indicators.note: to cook the books is to alter them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: rest of the fodder; 'with' joins the two

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: cook the cheese along with an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' belongs so naturally beside a cheese that it is easy to miss as the anagram signal; 'with' just adds ACTOR to IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this soft whey cheese is one of Italy's many cheeses.

clue.text: Signal is crude in every other place

indicators.note: taking a letter at every other position picks the 1st, 3rd and 5th

explanation.surface: A remark that a signal is crude wherever it shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In every other place' sounds like geography, but it is telling you to take alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: in theatre it is the signal telling an actor to come in.

clue.text: Sort out US city ignoring amendment initially

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so a letter goes
take the first letter of 'amendment'

blocks.note: first letter of amendment, removed from SEATTLE

explanation.surface: A plan to settle an American city's affairs without a constitutional amendment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amendment' tempts you toward US law, but only its first letter matters: A comes out of SEATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as when you resolve a dispute or pay off a bill.

clue.text: Nurse pocketing certain revolutionary’s box of goodies

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so TREAT holds the rest

blocks.note: to nurse a patient is to treat them; it goes around the rest
Che Guevara, the crossword's usual revolutionary, plus the 'S

explanation.surface: A nurse slipping a rebel's box of sweets into her pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' looks like a person doing the pocketing, but it is the verb for caring for a patient. Che Guevara was the Argentine-born guerrilla leader of the Cuban revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure chest is a box holding precious things, goodies.

clue.text: Loud noise and revelry periodically criminal

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter

explanation.surface: A noisy party that from time to time turns lawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' seems to describe how often the revelry turns criminal, but it picks out the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'revelry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer is a criminal who runs a dishonest racket.

clue.text: Lift up and tear down, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so go by the sound

blocks.note: to raze a building is to level it; say that verb and spell it the other way

explanation.surface: A builder's contradictory order to put something up and pull it down.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the two words sound identical yet mean opposite things: one builds up, the other knocks down.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you hoist a flag or lift up your hand.

clue.text: Fortress let acid out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or amiss, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Defenders of a castle pour acid down on attackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let acid out' reads as a siege tactic, and 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the stronghold guarding a city, as in Cairo or Quebec.

clue.text: Decide to put off something explosive

blocks.note: to deter is to put someone off
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to postpone a dangerous bomb disposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' reads as postpone; the wordplay wants its other sense, discourage.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being determined means having made up your mind.

clue.text: Quietly permitted to split separate dessert

indicators.note: to split something is to break into it, so the pair goes inside the word for separate

blocks.note: apart = separate; the outer part, AP…ART

explanation.surface: Someone is quietly allowed to divide up a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separate' looks like a verb for dividing the pudding, but it is an adjective, and the pair breaks in after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this fruit pie is one of countless desserts.

clue.text: Acclaim extremely practical inspection

indicators.note: take the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: an audit is an inspection of accounts

explanation.surface: Praise for an inspection that was thoroughly practical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'practical', but it asks for that word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually met in the plural: the praise heaped on a success.

clue.text: Puzzle observed after merry dance

indicators.note: after means following in order, so the word for observed is written behind the dance

blocks.note: a jig is a lively dance

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled by what they watched after a lively dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as someone puzzled by what they saw; 'Puzzle' is the definition, a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture puzzle cut into interlocking pieces.

clue.text: Technical language primarily just gas

indicators.note: first of all, so the first letter

explanation.surface: A put-down: technical language is mostly just hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' means empty talk in the surface, which is the joke; the wordplay wants a real gas, ARGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the insider vocabulary of a profession, usually said as a put-down.

clue.text: Cut off one very behind schedule

explanation.surface: A late-running train leaves one passenger stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is a pronoun in the surface and the Roman numeral I in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as when floods leave a village stranded.

clue.text: Immature insect right inside molten rock

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the letter for right goes into the rock

blocks.note: lava is molten rock; the outer part, LA…VA

explanation.surface: A grub trapped in molten rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like an adjective for the insect's position, but it is just the standard abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature stage of an insect, such as a caterpillar.

clue.text: Young woman at first orders cowboy’s accessory

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'orders'

explanation.surface: A young woman, at first, orders a cowboy's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' seems to say when she orders; it points at the O that begins 'orders'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is the looped rope a cowboy uses to catch cattle.

clue.text: Heads of secret aerospace lab dealing with rocket booster?

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

blocks.note: S, A, L: first letters of secret, aerospace, lab
addressing a problem is dealing with it

explanation.surface: A secret aerospace lab working on a rocket's booster stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket is a peppery salad leaf (arugula in the US), and a dressing boosts it; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad dressing livens up leaves such as rocket, so it is jokingly a rocket booster.

clue.text: Part of client’s falsehood

indicators.note: the answer is part of the next word

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of the word, between its C and NT'S

explanation.surface: A lawyer's client has told part of a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: A short hidden word sitting inside a single word of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: any deliberate untruth, from a fib to perjury.

clue.text: Anger about European flower arrangement

indicators.note: WRATH goes round, about, E

blocks.note: wrath = anger; the outer part, WR…ATH

explanation.surface: Rage over a continental floral display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' seems to mean concerning, but it tells WRATH to wrap round the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath is a ring of flowers or leaves.

clue.text: Juggling lemons is serious

indicators.note: juggled objects are tossed about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists that juggling lemons is no laughing matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is deliberately silly: juggling fruit is anything but serious.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a grave face or a formal occasion is serious in this sense.
